ember-orange.$description: Ember Orange — Orange supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

signal-blue.$description: Signal Blue — Links, secondary highlights, focus rings, decorative code accents — cool counterpoint to the warm orange, used sparingly

plex-green.$description: Plex Green — Green supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

plasma-magenta.$description: Plasma Magenta — Decorative code syntax highlight, studio editor token — appears only within code/editor contexts, not general UI

acid-lime.$description: Acid Lime — Code syntax token — restricted to developer-facing surfaces like the terminal and JSON editor

electric-blue.$description: Electric Blue — Code syntax token, inline link variants in editorial copy — secondary to Signal Blue

onyx.$description: Onyx — Primary text, dark hero backgrounds, dark product surface panels, button text on light fills

canvas-white.$description: Canvas White — Page background, card surfaces, text on dark sections, input fields

smoke.$description: Smoke — Borders, dividers, disabled text, muted icon strokes, placeholder text

ash.$description: Ash — Subtle borders on cards, input field outlines in light mode

graphite.$description: Graphite — Elevated dark surface (cards on dark backgrounds), input borders on dark sections

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Deepest elevated surface, code editor background, terminal panel

mid.$description: Mid — Secondary text, helper text, metadata, low-emphasis icons

steel.$description: Steel — Tertiary text, icon outlines on light surfaces

frost.$description: Frost — Hover backgrounds, subtle row separators, very light surface tint

waldenburg.$description: Primary display and body typeface. Used for all headings, body text, navigation, buttons, and editorial copy. The weight 425 is distinctive — a true book weight between 400 and 500 that adds warmth. Extremely tight letter-spacing at display sizes (–4.48px at 112px) creates a compressed, architectural feel. Custom stylistic alternates (cv01, cv11, cv12, cv13, ss07) give it a unique character — likely single-story 'a', distinctive 'g', and other bespoke glyphs.

ibm-plex-mono.$description: Monospace typeface for code blocks, terminal output, JSON schemas, numbered section labels (01–05), and technical metadata. Creates a developer-first identity when paired with Waldenburg's editorial warmth.
